page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfr6.2xlarge is an x86_64 compute-oriented virtual server belonging to the High Clock Speed instance family. It runs on the KVM hypervisor and is powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 3.1 GHz. The hardware configuration provides 8 vCPUs mapped across 4 dedicated physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Cache levels include 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a shared 35 MB L3 cache. It incorporates 64.0 GB of memory, equating to 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, and is provisioned with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. The instance includes no integrated local storage or discrete GPU accelerators, requiring external network block storage for persistence.

Benchmark evaluations position the ecs.hfr6.2xlarge consistently within the middle 50% across general-purpose metrics. It delivers a Geekbench single-core score of 1273.0 and a multi-core score of 4867.0, with a PassMark CPU score of 9028.43. Memory tests register 427.43 GB/sec in small-block cached read throughput and 50.86 GB/sec in large-block uncached read throughput. In application-focused metrics, it yields 7.55 million Redis SET operations per second and 7.51 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. CPU instruction sets include AVX-512 extensions (AVX-512F and AVX-512 VNNI), boosting compute operations and compilation workloads, which reached 7212.0 in Geekbench Clang tests.

Resource-density tradeoffs reflect its high clock-rate architecture paired with a generous 1:8 core-to-memory ratio. Without local NVMe drives, storage I/O relies entirely on cloud block attachments, which are limited by the 2 Gbps baseline network pipeline. Large language model inference reveals execution limits when scaling beyond small parameters: processing a 7B model dropped throughput into the bottom tier at 11.62 prompt tokens/sec and 6.44 generation tokens/sec. Consequently, ecs.hfr6.2xlarge functions best for in-memory caching systems, transactional databases, CI/CD compilation, and web serving clusters requiring strong per-thread frequencies alongside elevated memory allocation.
